metadata.note: The Mobile and Ohio main line through Tupelo -- the north-south half of the crossing that created the town, and the reason it is there at all: the place was settled as 'Gum Pond' along the M&O, founded 1860 and incorporated 1870. Chartered in 1848 to link the port of Mobile with the Ohio River, the M&O reached Columbus, Kentucky on Apr 22 1861. It merged with the Gulf, Mobile and Northern as the Gulf, Mobile and Ohio, effective 1940, whose Gulf Coast Rebel served Tupelo into the late 1950s. GM&O went into the Illinois Central Gulf in 1972. Only the Corinth-Tupelo-Meridian portion is drawn. See frisco_memphis_birmingham.geojson for the east-west line that crossed it.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_and_Ohio_Railroad (chartered January and February 1848 by Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee to span Mobile to the Ohio River near Cairo; first section Mobile to Citronelle opened 1852; reached Columbus, Kentucky Apr 22 1861 with steamboat connection to the Illinois Central at Cairo)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf,_Mobile_and_Ohio_Railroad (GM&O incorporated 1938 to merge the Gulf, Mobile and Northern and the Mobile and Ohio; named trains included the Gulf Coast Rebel, originally Mobile to Union, Mississippi, later extended to St. Louis; merged into the Illinois Central Aug 10 1972 forming the Illinois Central Gulf)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupelo,_Mississippi (Tupelo founded 1860, incorporated 1870, settled as 'Gum Pond' along the Mobile and Ohio Railroad; served into the late 1950s by the GM&O's Gulf Coast Rebel)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Headways are estimates and no timetable has been consulted. The 1958 end is NOT a documented last train: the only anchor is that the Gulf Coast Rebel served Tupelo 'into the late 1950s', and the documented end of passenger service in northeast Mississippi (Dec 9 1967) belongs to the Frisco's Southland on the other railroad, not to this one. When GM&O passenger service through Tupelo actually stopped is unknown. The 1861 start is when the M&O completed its through line to Kentucky; when track first reached Tupelo itself is not established, though the town was settled along the line by 1860. Only Corinth-Meridian is drawn, not the full Mobile-Columbus main line.

segments.note: Chartered in January and February 1848 by Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee to run from the port of Mobile to the Ohio River, the M&O opened its first stretch, Mobile to Citronelle, in 1852 and reached Columbus, Kentucky on Apr 22 1861, connecting there by steamboat to the Illinois Central at Cairo. Tupelo owes its existence to this line: the place was settled as 'Gum Pond' along the M&O, founded in 1860 and incorporated in 1870. Frequency estimated/unsourced

segments.note: The Gulf, Mobile and Ohio was incorporated in 1938 to merge the Gulf, Mobile and Northern with the Mobile and Ohio, taking effect in 1940. Into the late 1950s its Gulf Coast Rebel -- originally Mobile to Union, Mississippi, later extended to St. Louis -- was still calling at Tupelo. GM&O merged into the Illinois Central on Aug 10 1972 to form the Illinois Central Gulf; the line is CPKC freight today. Frequency estimated/unsourced
